title.narrative: West Bank Protection Consortium fas II
West Bank Protection Consortium phase II

description.narrative:
The main goal of the WBPC as a consortium is to prevent, mitigate and respond to the forcible transfer of Palestinian households and communities in the West Bank and East Jerusalem. This can be reached by ensuring that: • Palestinian households and communities meet their basic needs and recover from international humanitarian law and human rights law violations. • Vulnerable Palestinian households and communities are protected and prepared against potential international humanitarian law and human rights law violations. • Vulnerable Palestinian households and communities have access to basic services and economic opportunities for empowerment, resilience and selfdevelopment. • Local and governmental Palestinian authorities have their capacities reinforced. • Duty bearers are accountable and face up to their responsibilities
The West Bank Protection Consortium was established in 2015 and brings together five Consortium partners: Action Against Hunger, Acted, Norwegian Refugee Council, Premiere Urgence International and We World. These are all international nongovernmental organisations that are well established in Palestine. They have experience both of emergency assistance, as well as resilience work, each one with their own focus. This makes them well positioned for smooth transition along the humanitarian, resilience, and development nexus, when circumstances allow. The main focus of the consortium is humanitarian assistance to people in Area C who are subject to violence, forced removals and setllement expansion. The Consortium is funded by the European Civil Protection and Humanitarian Aid Operations (ECHO) and 13 donor states. The consortium operate within three different pillars 1) Emergency Releif 2) Resilience Building and 3) Adovacy. The emergency releif is by far the largest pillar. The proposed project is meant to provide further resources into the Resilience Building pillar (2), to ensure that at risk communities have access to basic services, economic opportunities and legal aid. Strengthening their resilience and providing basic development through a Nexus approach is critical for people to be able to live on their lands. While this specific project aims to reduce the need for emergency assistance in the long run, it is designed to operate in conjunction with and be supported by the WBPC's emergency response mechanisms (pillar I) ensuring a comprehensive approach to both resilience and crisis response. The project seeks to prevent the forcible transfer of Palestinians from isolated Area C areas, by increasing their resilience and independence. This will be done through strengthening community infrastructure and access to basic services, empowering households with sustainable income resources and advocy for human rights. The West Bank Protection Consortium's integrated protection approach is designed to counter the multifaceted drivers that contribute to the risk of forcible transfer of Palestinian communities. This approach recognizes that forcible transfer is not a singular event, but rather the culmination of a complex interplay between vulnerabilities within the micro environment and pressures exerted by the macro environment.
